question: An analog clock starts at midnight and runs for \(2025\) minutes before stopping. What is the tangent of the acute angle between the hour hand and the minute hand when the clock stops?
solution:
The hands repeat their positions every twelve hours, so first reduce the elapsed time to a clock reading.

Since
\[
2025=33\cdot60+45,
\]
the clock stops after \(33\) hours and \(45\) minutes, showing \(9{:}45\). The minute hand points directly at \(9\). Each hour mark spans \(360^\circ/12=30^\circ\), and the hour hand has moved three quarters of the way from \(9\) to \(10\). The acute angle is therefore
\[
\theta=\frac34\cdot30^\circ=22.5^\circ.
\]
Because \(2\theta=45^\circ\), the identities
\[
\cos 2\theta=2\cos^2\theta-1,
\qquad \sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1
\]
give
\[
\cos^2\theta=\frac{1+\cos45^\circ}{2},
\qquad
\sin^2\theta=\frac{1-\cos45^\circ}{2}.
\]
Using \(\tan\theta=\sin\theta/\cos\theta\) and \(\cos45^\circ=\sqrt2/2\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tan^2\theta
&=\frac{1-\sqrt2/2}{1+\sqrt2/2}\\
&=\frac{2-\sqrt2}{2+\sqrt2}\\
&=3-2\sqrt2=(\sqrt2-1)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The tangent is positive because \(\theta\) is acute. Hence the answer is \(\boxed{\sqrt2-1}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Once the clock angle is found, an angle bisector in an isosceles right triangle gives its tangent through side lengths.

The elapsed time is \(33\) hours and \(45\) minutes, so the clock shows \(9{:}45\). Its minute hand points at \(9\), while its hour hand lies three quarters of the way from \(9\) to \(10\). Since consecutive hour marks are \(30^\circ\) apart, the acute angle is
\[
\frac34\cdot30^\circ=22.5^\circ.
\]
Consider a triangle \(ABC\) with a right angle at \(C\) and legs \(AC=BC=1\). Its two other angles are \(45^\circ\), and the Pythagorean theorem gives \(AB=\sqrt2\).

Let the bisector of \(\angle A\) meet \(BC\) at \(D\). Then \(\angle CAD=22.5^\circ\). The angle bisector theorem says that an internal angle bisector divides the opposite side in the ratio of the adjacent sides. Here it gives
\[
\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{AB}{AC}=\sqrt2.
\]
Since \(BD+DC=BC=1\), we have
\[
DC=\frac{1}{1+\sqrt2}=\sqrt2-1.
\]
Triangle \(ACD\) is right at \(C\), so
\[
\tan22.5^\circ=\frac{DC}{AC}=\boxed{\sqrt2-1}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutionMethods.label: Bisect a right triangle
